title: Quiz: Reactions of Acids with Metal Oxides

questions.stem: What are the products when an acid reacts with a metal oxide?
questions.explanation: When an acid reacts with a metal oxide, the products are a salt and water: acid + metal oxide → salt + water. This is a type of neutralisation reaction.

questions.stem: What salt is formed when copper oxide reacts with sulfuric acid?
questions.explanation: Copper oxide + sulfuric acid → copper sulfate + water. The copper comes from the metal oxide and the sulfate comes from sulfuric acid.

questions.stem: Why are reactions between acids and metal oxides classified as neutralisation reactions?

options.text: Because the metal oxide acts as a base, neutralising the acid

questions.explanation: Metal oxides are bases -- they react with acids to form a salt and water. Since a base is neutralising the acid, this is a neutralisation reaction.

questions.stem: What observation indicates that black copper oxide has reacted with warm dilute sulfuric acid?

options.text: The black powder disappears and the solution turns blue

questions.explanation: When black copper oxide reacts with sulfuric acid, the black solid dissolves and the solution turns blue due to the formation of copper sulfate, which is a blue solution.

questions.stem: Which of the following is the correct word equation for zinc oxide reacting with hydrochloric acid?

options.text: Zinc oxide + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + hydrogen
Zinc oxide + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + water
Zinc oxide + hydrochloric acid → zinc nitrate + water
Zinc oxide + hydrochloric acid → zinc sulfate + water

questions.explanation: Zinc oxide + hydrochloric acid → zinc chloride + water. Metal oxide + acid always gives a salt and water. Hydrochloric acid produces chloride salts.

questions.stem: How do you know when excess metal oxide has been added to an acid?

options.text: Unreacted solid remains at the bottom after the reaction stops

questions.explanation: When excess metal oxide is added, all the acid is used up but some solid metal oxide remains unreacted at the bottom of the container, showing that excess has been added.

questions.stem: Which metal oxide would you use with nitric acid to make magnesium nitrate?
questions.explanation: Magnesium oxide + nitric acid → magnesium nitrate + water. To make a magnesium salt, you need to start with a magnesium compound (magnesium oxide).
